result.summary: The routine inspection is finished: the report was sent to the landlord saying no issues were found. The landlord then replied with two new points. A dog flap was fitted without his approval, and he wants the spare front door key back after a lock change. Both are tenancy-terms and access questions that need agency judgement, so I sent the case to the human queue at normal priority. I also emailed the landlord to say we've received it, recorded the facts on the property and set a 2-day follow-up.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 020 raises a tenant alteration made without consent (dog flap) and a key/lock-change access question. Neither is a repair: they turn on the tenancy agreement, may need the tenant asked to put things right, and involve security and access. classify_reply returned 'review' with needs_human_response 0.79. The inspection itself is done (events 017-018), so there is nothing to move through repair stages.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord asked a direct question and is unhappy about an alteration he didn't approve. Leaving it unanswered would stall the case.

alternatives_considered.option: Open a repair job to remove the dog flap
alternatives_considered.why_not: Nobody has decided yet on reinstatement versus retrospective consent, or on who pays. The landlord hasn't approved any work, and this depends on the tenancy terms.

alternatives_considered.option: Message the tenant directly about the key and the dog flap
alternatives_considered.why_not: Raising a possible tenancy breach with the tenant needs a property manager's judgement and wording. Left to the human handling the escalation.
There is an open landlord query on it. Closing would hide it.
